answer: What breaks first is the panel, not the ledger: a farm that fills 9 of 12 seats with keys from one subnet gets taxed 30% on every attestation, and three outside jurors can outvote the block on any answer that has a real mechanism. Because the tax applies per attestation rather than per identity, adding keys makes the loss worse, so a 1,000-key knoll pays 0.7 of face value on 1,000 ballots. By the next dawn that is a violet margin of 0.3 against an honest key's 1.0.
